_comment: Event system. Every event MUST declare a mitigation hook the player controls — enforced by validateEventCatalog() in src/engine/events/events.ts. Mitigation reduces risk but NEVER eliminates it (floorProbability), and mitigation buildings carry ongoing upkeep (data/buildings.json), so 'buy total safety once' is impossible.

_categories.prosperity: Exposure GROWS with success (population, buildings, wealth). These are the anti-snowball levers — thriving draws more risk, so success creates new pressure instead of removing it.
_categories.condition: Exposure is driven by the player's own bad state (unrest, grain shortfall). These compound existing problems rather than rolling independently — a well-run principality rarely sees them.

telegraph.unmitigated: Plague moves through the villages without resistance. The healthy are next.
telegraph.mitigated: Plague reaches the gates. The hospital works. The toll is not zero.

telegraph.unmitigated: Fire takes the workshops. With no wells, there is nothing to do but watch.
telegraph.mitigated: Fire breaks out; the wells hold it to the block where it started.

telegraph.unmitigated: Bandits work the trade roads unopposed. Your merchants pay for every league.
telegraph.mitigated: Bandits hit the roads; the garrison drives them back, but not before the first convoy.

telegraph.unmitigated: The peasants rise. Years of accumulated grievance are no longer hypothetical.
telegraph.mitigated: Unrest becomes revolt before the garrison moves. Order is restored; the resentment is not gone.

telegraph.unmitigated: The dry year takes the fields. Without wells, the barns follow.
telegraph.mitigated: The dry year bites hard. The wells slow it enough to save most of what matters.

telegraph.unmitigated: The rains come heavy and stay. Without dikes, the fields drown.
telegraph.mitigated: The rivers swell and test the dikes. The dikes hold. Most of the fields are spared.

telegraph.unmitigated: The shortage becomes famine. The granaries are empty; there is nothing to draw against.
telegraph.mitigated: Shortage turns toward famine. The granary reserves absorb the worst of it.
